title: Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) D(Dic_12) Tham 5.11 floating-point check
question: Check whether the R1-normalized Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) presentation, interpreted upside-down in the Tham 5.11 context with two original 3-handles contributing D^-2, reproduces the standard CP2 +1-framed Omega unknot value for untwisted D(Dic_12) and for the pointed witness character powers.

context.category: untwisted Drinfeld double D(Dic_12), also recorded earlier as D(Dic_3)/Q12 convention
context.why_this_category: Previous split CP2#2CPbar scans found a nontrivial pointed witness g=(a^3, chi), chi(a)=-1, chi(x)=i, with theta(g)=-1.
context.yasui_input: R1-normalized Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) braid, component order in braid A,C,B, total framings 4,4,1.
context.tham511_interpretation: The two original 3-handles are read upside-down as two Tham 5.11 one-handle operations, giving normalization by D^2. There are no special dotted knots in this input, so no cut-and-vacuum projection is applied.
context.h2_character_rule: H2 generator h pulls back to A=2h, C=2h, B=h in braid order A,C,B; for witness h_power=a use component powers (2a,2a,a) modulo 4.

artifacts.role: floating-point manifest, profiling, range aggregate, and combine script
four compact rank-range aggregate worker outputs
combined comparison against standard CP2 +1 framed Omega unknot

runtime_notes.previous_figure3_dic12_history: The earlier Yasui Figure 3 D(Dic_12) run required priority scheduling and distributed workers; historical profiling estimated hours on a single worker for the remaining tail.
runtime_notes.singleton_json_route_note: An initial fat singleton JSON route was interrupted after 1302 chunks because per-sector metadata and repeated MTC sha256 hashing dominated runtime. The pass result uses compact range aggregates, not the partial singleton chunks.

claim_boundary: This is a floating-point computational consistency check for the current Yasui Figure 2 PD/braid convention and Tham 5.11 upside-down working interpretation. It is not a theorem, not an exact arithmetic certificate, and not an exotic-pair separation claim.
